text: The maximum offered for Commercial property is Total insured value (TIV) up to $25,000,000 per account and $10,000,000 per location [HM-1.1]
The maximum offered for General liability is $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate standard; up to $2,000,000 / $4,000,000 with Senior Underwriter approval [HM-1.1]
**TIV (total insured value)**: building replacement cost plus business personal property plus 12 months of business income, summed over all locations. [HM-1.2]
**Experience period**: the 5 most recent complete policy years before the proposed effective date. [HM-1.2]
**Large loss**: a single claim with incurred loss of $250,000 or more. [HM-1.2]
The applicant has been in business for at least 3 years under the same ownership, or has prior experience of at least 3 years in the same operations documented in the submission. [HM-2.1]
Every building was built in 1950 or later, or has had its roof, electrical, plumbing and heating systems updated within the last 25 years (with the year of each update documented). [HM-2.1]
Roofs are 20 years old or less at the proposed effective date. [HM-2.1]
Every location is in public protection class 1 to 8. [HM-2.1]
A submission failing item 1, 3 or 4 is referred to a Senior Underwriter. [HM-2.1]
A submission failing item 2 or 5 is referred to the Underwriting Manager. [HM-2.1]
A submission failing item 6 is handled under HM-2.2. [HM-2.1]
buildings vacant or unoccupied for more than 60 consecutive days; [HM-2.2]
nightclubs and bars with a licensed occupancy above 300 persons; [HM-2.2]
restaurants with deep-fat frying, unless every cooking line has an automatic fire suppression system inspected within the last 6 months; [HM-2.3]
habitational buildings of more than 4 stories; [HM-2.3]
warehouses larger than 100,000 square feet; [HM-2.3]

a beneficial ownership statement listing every individual owning 25% or more of each named insured. [HM-3.1]
any location with TIV above $5,000,000: an inspection report dated within 12 months; [HM-3.1]
Loss runs must cover every line being quoted for each of the 5 years of the experience period, plus the current policy term to date. [HM-3.2]
Each loss run must be valued (its "valued as of" date) no more than 90 days before the proposed effective date. [HM-3.2]
An applicant with fewer than 3 years of loss history (for example a new venture) is referred to a Senior Underwriter. [HM-3.2]
For every claim, paid loss plus case reserve must equal incurred loss within $1.00. [HM-3.3]
A difference in claim count, or a difference in total incurred loss of more than 10.0%, is a referral to a Senior Underwriter. [HM-3.3]
Every claim of $250,000 or more incurred must have a written description of the cause of loss and the corrective actions taken. [HM-3.3]
Each claim is capped at $250,000 for loss ratio purposes. [HM-4.1]
The 5-year loss ratio = sum of capped incurred losses over the 5 years / sum of earned premiums over the 5 years. [HM-4.1]
The current, incomplete term is excluded from the 5-year loss ratio but is reviewed for large losses. [HM-4.1]
If earned premium for any year of the experience period is missing, the 5-year loss ratio is not calculated and the submission is placed in "request more information" status. [HM-4.1]
The treatment for 55.0% or less is Acceptable [HM-4.2]
The treatment for More than 55.0% and up to 70.0% is Refer to a Senior Underwriter [HM-4.2]
The treatment for More than 70.0% is Refer to the Underwriting Manager, who either approves an exception backed by documented remediation (HM-9.4) or confirms a decline-for-review [HM-4.2]
In addition, any single annual loss ratio above 100.0% within the experience period is a referral to a Senior Underwriter, whatever the 5-year loss ratio is. [HM-4.2]
3 or more property claims with a date of loss in any rolling 12-month period; [HM-4.3]
4 or more general liability claims in the experience period; [HM-4.3]
any large loss ($250,000 or more incurred) in the experience period or the current term; [HM-4.3]
a rising frequency trend: more claims in the 2 most recent policy years than in the 3 policy years before them combined. [HM-4.3]

For every location the property schedule must show: street address, construction class, occupancy, year built, year of roof replacement, number of stories, total square feet, sprinkler status, building replacement cost, business personal property value and 12-month business income value. [HM-5.1]
The schedule must be signed and dated by the applicant no more than 12 months before the proposed effective date. [HM-5.1]
The treatment for 5.0% or less is Use the property schedule TIV [HM-5.2]
The treatment for More than 5.0% and up to 15.0% is Request a corrected application or schedule [HM-5.2]
The treatment for More than 15.0% is Refer to a Senior Underwriter [HM-5.2]

Contractors that subcontract more than 50% of their work must provide evidence of certificate-of-insurance tracking for their subcontractors; without it the submission is referred to a Senior Underwriter. [HM-7.1]
Every individual owning 25% or more of each named insured must be identified (HM-3.1 item 6). [HM-8.1]

**Principal**: any individual who owns 20% or more of the applicant, or who is the control person. [NBC-1.2]
**Beneficial owner**: any individual who directly or indirectly owns 25% or more of the applicant. [NBC-1.2]
**Control person**: one individual with significant responsibility to manage the applicant (for example the CEO, managing member or general partner). [NBC-1.2]
**Verified annual revenue**: the sum of eligible deposits over the most recent 12 consecutive months of bank statements. [NBC-1.2]

The applicant is a corporation, limited liability company or partnership organized in a US state and has been in operation for at least 24 months, measured from the formation date on its formation documents. [NBC-2.1]
Verified annual revenue is at least $250,000. [NBC-2.1]
Every principal has a personal credit score of at least 660 from the credit report pulled for this application. [NBC-2.1]
Neither the applicant nor any principal has had a bankruptcy discharge or dismissal within the last 7 years. [NBC-2.1]

Near misses may be considered through the exceptions process (NBC-7.4): time in business of at least 18 months (item 1), verified annual revenue of at least $225,000 (item 2), or a principal credit score of at least 640 (item 3). [NBC-2.1]
An application that fails item 4, 5 or 6 cannot be approved through an exception. [NBC-2.1]
cannabis or marijuana cultivation, processing, distribution or retail, including businesses that derive more than 10% of revenue from cannabis-related customers; [NBC-2.2]
restaurants and bars in operation for less than 36 months; [NBC-2.3]
businesses with more than 30% of revenue from a single customer (customer concentration). [NBC-2.3]
the 12 most recent consecutive months of statements for every business operating account, with the most recent statement ending no more than 60 days before the application date; [NBC-3.1]
business federal tax returns for the two most recent tax years; [NBC-3.1]
a year-to-date profit and loss statement and balance sheet dated no more than 90 days before the application date; [NBC-3.1]
requests above $500,000: financial statements for the most recent fiscal year reviewed or audited by an independent CPA; [NBC-3.1]
Add up all deposits to every business operating account for each of the 12 most recent consecutive months. [NBC-3.2]
Verified annual revenue is the sum over the 12 months. [NBC-3.2]
Verified average monthly revenue is verified annual revenue divided by 12. [NBC-3.2]
If statements cover fewer than 12 months, revenue is not verified and the file is placed in "request more information" status for the missing months (NBC-3.5). [NBC-3.2]

A deposit is treated as a transfer when the statement description names another account of the applicant or an owner, or when a withdrawal of the same amount from another applicant account appears within 2 business days. [NBC-3.3]
**Non-operating one-time receipts**: tax refunds, insurance claim payments, legal settlements, proceeds from the sale of assets, and government grants or relief funds. [NBC-3.3]
Cash deposits: in any month, eligible cash deposits are capped at 25% of that month's eligible non-cash deposits, so cash is never more than 20% of the month's eligible deposits. [NBC-3.3]
The classification for 10.0% or less is Benign [NBC-3.4]
The classification for More than 10.0% and up to 25.0% is Explainable discrepancy [NBC-3.4]
The classification for More than 25.0% is Unsupported discrepancy [NBC-3.4]
any missing statement month within the required 12 consecutive months (request the missing statements); [NBC-3.5]
more than 6 non-sufficient-funds (NSF) or overdraft events in the most recent 6 months; [NBC-3.5]
3 or more months, within the most recent 12, that end with a negative balance; [NBC-3.5]
an average daily balance over the most recent 3 months that is below 5% of the proposed monthly payment multiplied by 12 (that is, below 5% of proposed annual debt service). [NBC-3.5]

**Net operating income (NOI)** is earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) from the trailing-twelve-month profit and loss statement, with one adjustment: if verified annual revenue is lower than the revenue on that profit and loss statement, NOI is reduced dollar for dollar by the difference. [NBC-4.1]

existing debt service: 12 times the total monthly payments on all business debt that will remain after closing, taking for each debt the higher of the payment on the debt schedule and the payment seen in the bank statements. [NBC-4.1]
term and equipment loans: 12 times the fully amortizing monthly payment at the note rate and term; [NBC-4.1]
lines of credit: 12 months of interest at the note rate on the full committed amount, plus 10% of the committed amount. [NBC-4.1]
The minimum decision dscr for Term loan is 1.25 [NBC-4.2]
The minimum decision dscr for Equipment loan is 1.25 [NBC-4.2]
The minimum decision dscr for Revolving line of credit is 1.35 [NBC-4.2]
below the product minimum and at least 1.10: refer to a Senior Underwriter; approval requires at least two compensating factors from NBC-4.3 and is recorded as a policy exception; [NBC-4.2]
below 1.10: does not meet policy; the file can only be approved by the Credit Committee as a policy exception, otherwise it is referred for a decline-for-review decision. [NBC-4.2]
business liquidity (cash and equivalents in the business accounts at the most recent statement date) of at least 6 months of proposed debt service; [NBC-4.3]
global DSCR of at least 1.50, combining the business with the personal income and debts of all guarantors; [NBC-4.3]
collateral coverage (NBC-5.1) of at least 1.50; [NBC-4.3]
time in business of at least 10 years; [NBC-4.3]
every principal has a credit score of at least 760; [NBC-4.3]
Total business debt after closing divided by NOI (NBC-4.1) must be 4.00 or less. [NBC-4.4]
Above 4.00 is a referral to a Senior Underwriter. [NBC-4.4]

Stacking: 2 or more new loans or merchant cash advance fundings in the most recent 90 days of statements is a referral to a Senior Underwriter. 3 or more is not eligible for standard processing and is referred to the Chief Credit Officer. [NBC-4.4]
Every term and equipment loan above $100,000 and every line of credit is stress tested: [NBC-4.5]
Revenue stress: reduce verified annual revenue by 20%, reduce NOI by the same dollar amount, and recalculate DSCR. [NBC-4.5]
A stressed DSCR below 1.00 is a referral to a Senior Underwriter. [NBC-4.5]
Rate stress (variable-rate products only): add 2.00 percentage points to the note rate and recalculate proposed debt service. [NBC-4.5]
A stressed DSCR below 1.10 is a referral to a Senior Underwriter. [NBC-4.5]
Collateral is required for every request above $250,000. [NBC-5.1]
Requests of $250,000 or less may be unsecured. [NBC-5.1]

The maximum advance rate for New equipment is 80% [NBC-5.1]
The maximum advance rate for Used equipment is 60% [NBC-5.1]

The maximum advance rate for Inventory (finished goods) is 50% [NBC-5.1]
Secured requests need collateral coverage of at least 1.00. [NBC-5.1]
Coverage below 1.00 and at least 0.80 is a referral to a Senior Underwriter. [NBC-5.1]
Coverage below 0.80 cannot be approved without a policy exception from the Credit Committee. [NBC-5.1]
Personal guarantees: every principal who owns 20% or more must sign an unconditional personal guarantee. [NBC-5.1]
The applicant must identify every beneficial owner (25% or more) and one control person, and certify the information in the beneficial ownership certification. [NBC-6.1]
Ownership percentages disclosed on the application must add up to 100%, and must match the formation documents. [NBC-6.1]

A difference of more than 5 percentage points for any owner, or owners in the formation documents who are missing from the application, is a referral to a Senior Underwriter and to KYC Operations. [NBC-6.1]
the residential address must be verified by the credit report or a utility bill dated within 90 days. [NBC-6.2]
screening is run at application and again within 5 business days before closing; [NBC-6.3]
Adverse media searches cover the applicant and every principal for the most recent 7 years. [NBC-6.4]
Credible adverse media (reported by at least one established news organization or found in a court or regulatory record) in a relevant category is referred to Compliance. [NBC-6.4]
